questions.text: It's your cousin's Sangeet and your family is putting up a group performance. What is your role?

options.A: Being the star performer in the center, hitting all the energetic hook steps flawlessly.
options.B: Patiently correcting your cousins' hand angles and footwork so the group doesn't look completely clumsy.
options.C: Mixing the audio track, deciding the V-formations, and visualizing the entire stage entry.
options.D: Making sure everyone actually shows up for practice, arranging the props, and coordinating with the DJ.

questions.text: You are making a dance reel on a trending Bollywood song with your friends. What's your focus?

options.A: Giving killer expressions and throwing in a backflip or heavy energy to grab all the attention.
options.B: Breaking down the complex trending step logically so your untalented friends can actually match the beat.
options.C: Directing the phone camera angles, choosing matching aesthetic outfits, and deciding the background location.
options.D: Using the exact trending audio, adding the right hashtags, and forcing everyone to share it to get maximum views.

questions.text: Your school is participating in a huge Inter-School Dance Competition. What are you doing?

options.A: Practicing your solo spin and jumping sequence for hours until your feet physically hurt.
options.B: Watching the rehearsal video on repeat to point out exactly who is a micro-second out of sync.
options.C: Coming up with a powerful, emotional theme (like 'Tribute to the Army' or 'Save Water') for the performance.
options.D: Handling the permission slips, collecting the costume money from everyone, and talking to the teachers.

questions.text: When you sit with your family to watch Dance India Dance or Dance+, what do you focus on?

options.A: Getting goosebumps seeing the dancer's raw stamina, flexibility, and stage presence.
options.B: Listening closely to Remo D'Souza or Terence Lewis when they point out flawed classical footwork or bad posture.
options.C: Admiring the storytelling, the lighting, the background dancers, and how the entire act was visually designed.
options.D: Wondering how much the winner gets paid, the sponsors behind the show, and how they build their brand after winning.

questions.text: The elder uncles and aunties want to dance at a family function but they have no rhythm. How do you handle them?

options.A: Jumping into the circle with them, matching their crazy energy, and hyping them up so they feel like stars.
options.B: Teaching them a very simple '1-2-3-4' side-step and clapping on beat so they stay in rhythm.
options.C: Giving them funny, dramatic Bollywood steps (like the classic 'changing the lightbulb') so the performance looks entertaining.
options.D: Politely managing the timeline so they don't hog the stage all night and the actual planned performances can happen.

questions.text: You hear a massive hit song like 'Naatu Naatu' or 'Chaleya' playing loudly in a car. What happens?

options.A: You literally cannot stop your body from grooving; you start doing the hook step right there in your seat.
options.B: You mentally analyze how difficult the leg movement is and figure out the exact body mechanics required to do it.
options.C: You close your eyes and imagine a completely different, unique choreography for the same song.
options.D: You note how viral the song is and immediately think about using it as the finale song for your society's Diwali fest.

questions.text: It's the school Annual Day function. Where are you?

options.A: On the main stage, center-front, doing the most energetic Bhangra or Hip-Hop solo of the night.
options.B: Sitting in the front row during dress rehearsals, strictly shouting out instructions to keep the lines straight.
options.C: In the green room, styling the dancers in traditional-to-modern fusion costumes you picked out yourself.
options.D: Backstage with a walkie-talkie, ensuring the mics work, the music plays on cue, and the next batch is ready.

questions.text: Your dance group is really struggling with a fast, complicated 8-count step. How do you solve it?

options.A: You keep repeating the routine physically, pushing your body through the sweat until you get it perfect.
options.B: You slow the song down to 0.5x speed, break the beat into '1-and-2-and', and explain the exact weight-shift required.
options.C: You change the complicated step into something simpler that looks equally beautiful and fits the music perfectly.
options.D: You tell everyone to take a 10-minute water break and have a quick pep talk to boost their crashing morale.

questions.text: During the neighborhood Ganesh Chaturthi or Durga Puja, what is your main contribution?

options.A: Leading the Garba or Lezim circle with non-stop, intense energy for three hours straight.
options.B: Ensuring the younger kids know the actual traditional meaning and the authentic hand gestures of the folk dance.
options.C: Creating a grand, dramatic entry sequence for the society's cultural night that will shock all the aunties.
options.D: Going door-to-door to collect 'chanda' (funds) to pay for the massive DJ and stage setup.

questions.text: Honestly, what is the best part about dance for you?

options.A: The absolute adrenaline rush of hearing the crowd scream when you hit a perfect jump or split.
options.B: The discipline of mastering your physical body and passing on that exact perfection to your students.
options.C: Taking an empty stage and painting a beautiful, emotional story using bodies, expressions, and music.
options.D: Building a massive community of dancers, putting up grand shows, and making it a highly successful business.

Lead_Dancer.title: The Spotlight Star (Lead Dancer / Stage Performer)
Lead_Dancer.primary_match_text: You are pure energy, stamina, and expression! You love the adrenaline of being on stage and having all eyes on you. In the professional world, you would be the Lead Dancer performing in live concerts, Bollywood movies, or massive theatrical shows.
Lead_Dancer.day_in_the_life: Your day starts with intense physical conditioning and stretching. You spend hours in the studio sweating it out, rehearsing for a massive live concert where you will perform alongside a famous Bollywood star in front of thousands of screaming fans.
Lead_Dancer.alternative_match_text: If not a professional dancer, you would excel as an Actor, Fitness Model, or a Stunt Performer.
Lead_Dancer.roadmap: Take Any Stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a BPA (Bachelor of Performing Arts) in Dance. Join reputed companies as a company dancer (like Shiamak Davar's Dance Company or Ashley Lobo's Navdhara). Keep giving physical auditions for reality shows and music videos.

Dance_Instructor.title: The Perfectionist Guru (Dance Technique Instructor)
Dance_Instructor.primary_match_text: You have a highly analytical mind and a deep respect for discipline! You understand the mechanics, history, and exact angles of movement. As an Instructor, you don't just dance; you break down complex techniques to mold beginners into flawless professionals.
Dance_Instructor.day_in_the_life: You are in a mirrored studio, observing your students closely. You break down a complex Kathak spin or a Hip-Hop isolation, correcting their posture, counting the beats aloud, and pushing them to achieve absolute technical perfection.
Dance_Instructor.alternative_match_text: If not a Dance Instructor, you would make an amazing Physical Education (PT) Teacher, Physiotherapist, or Yoga Guru.
Dance_Instructor.roadmap: Take Any Stream in 11th/12th. For Classical: Complete your Visharad or Alankar (through Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya). For Western: Get certified through international boards (like ISTD London) or intensive programs at Terence Lewis Professional Training Institute (TLPTI).

Choreographer.title: The Visionary Director (Choreographer)
Choreographer.primary_match_text: You are the creative mastermind! You see dance as a canvas for storytelling. You don't just perform the steps; you create them. As a Choreographer, you visualize the formations, design the emotional arc of the routine, and direct the dancers to bring your vision to life.
Choreographer.day_in_the_life: You sit with music directors and film directors to understand the vibe of a new song. You experiment with movements in an empty studio, teach the final hook steps to the lead actors, and direct the camera angles on the film set to make the dance look cinematic.
Choreographer.alternative_match_text: If not a Choreographer, you would thrive as a Film Director, Creative Director, or Fashion Show Director.
Choreographer.roadmap: Take Any Stream in 11th/12th (Arts/Humanities is great for creative thinking). Pursue a BA/BPA in Dance or Mass Media. Gain heavy experience by assisting established Bollywood or commercial choreographers. Short courses in film direction or cinematography are a massive bonus.

Dance_Academy_Owner.title: The Studio Boss (Dance Academy Owner / Event Organizer)
Dance_Academy_Owner.primary_match_text: You are a born leader and entrepreneur! You see dance not just as an art form, but as a massive, booming business. As a Dance Academy Owner or Event Organizer, you would manage the studio, hire the best instructors, organize mega-events, and build a profitable fitness and art brand.
Dance_Academy_Owner.day_in_the_life: You are not just dancing; you are running an empire. You negotiate rental spaces for your new studio branch, run Instagram marketing campaigns to get new admissions, manage the payroll for your instructors, and pitch sponsorship deals for your academy's annual showcase.
Dance_Academy_Owner.alternative_match_text: If not in the Dance industry, you would be a brilliant Event Manager, Talent Manager, or Startup Founder.
Dance_Academy_Owner.roadmap: Take Commerce in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA, B.Com, or Event Management degree. While you should learn dance to understand the product, your ultimate goal should be an MBA or a Diploma in Entrepreneurship to help you scale your academy into a national franchise.
